purpose: Honest disclosure of every residual risk this phase is aware of, per its own no-self-certification discipline (Section 32/35: this phase may only report REMEDIATED_PENDING_INDEPENDENT_RECERTIFICATION, never CERTIFIED).
primaryRisk: NONE of the 11 fixes in this phase has been independently verified by anyone other than the workstream that wrote it. Every disposition below is self-reported by the fixing workstream. The next phase (3F.1.6.RC, Targeted Foundation Recertification) exists specifically to close this gap and is the only phase authorized to use the word CERTIFIED for any of these 11 items.

perBlockerResidualRisks.risk: The new positive-evidence heuristic (paragraph break / sentence-terminal punctuation / ARTICLE-adjacency) was validated against a 23-case false-negative guard plus the 7 known real anomalies, but has not been tested against a genuinely unseen document's formatting conventions - a document with none of these 3 positive signals for a legitimate heading (e.g. no paragraph breaks at all due to poor OCR, no terminal punctuation, and not ARTICLE-adjacent) could still be missed. This is the same class of risk BLOCKER-1 was originally created to close, now at one remove.

Workstream A's fixes reuse existing taxonomies correctly, but the supersession-awareness audit (05-supersession-certification.json) named 2 named consumers plus a broader population; this phase's fix targeted the specific consumers/mechanisms the 5 named blockers described, not a from-scratch re-audit of every possible current-state consumer in the codebase. A genuinely new consumer added in a future phase could still bypass supersession awareness if it doesn't route through the now-fixed shared helpers.

Explicitly disclosed by Workstream E itself: DefinedTermNode.stableKey (a separate table from the ContractRule.definedTermRefs this blocker fixed) is independently stale for the same two real companies, in a pre-P0-2 format missing documentId. getRuleSourceTrace's definedTerms lookup will still return empty for these companies until that distinct, out-of-scope defect is separately backfilled. Recommended as its own future follow-up, not attempted here.

Explicitly disclosed by Workstream B: same-family fused claims (e.g. two different Indebtedness baskets bundled in one sentence without lettering) remain a residual identity-collision risk - the fix's findCoordinateClauseSplit only splits when each side of a coordinate clause matches a DIFFERENT covenant family, by design (to avoid over-splitting genuinely single claims), so same-family bundling is a known, covered-by-a-guarded-test-but-unfixed gap.

The fix closes the specific single-marker/single-condition drafting pattern this workstream's fault-injection proved was missed, tested against 9 condition-phrasing forms. A condition phrased in a form none of the 9 forms or the existing 77 pre-existing verifier tests anticipate could still be missed - the fix widens recall, it does not achieve exhaustive coverage of all possible condition phrasings.

Explicitly disclosed by Workstream F: compiled semantic IR (IRRule/IRDefinition) has no durable persistence anywhere in this codebase, by the compiler's own pre-existing design (deferred to a future phase) - this phase's live orchestrator correctly wires the flow through to AnalysisRun/ClaimReviewItem persistence, but a fully re-runnable, queryable history of every compiled rule's own IR is not yet part of the live product. Additionally, the orchestrator's own golden E2E test exercises one representative real-document path; it has not been run against FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR at full package scale through the new live boundary (that would require re-running this phase's own known-package regression through the NEW orchestrator specifically, which was not done - the known-package regression in 22-known-package-regression.json still uses the older, direct-pipeline-call pattern, not the new live orchestrator).

This is an architecture-scope decision, not a code fix - the underlying invariant #35 concern (competing truth logs must be explicitly reconciled) remains permanently true and enforced as FUTURE_ENFORCED for this specific example; if a future phase (Phase 6) implements DebtEvent creation from a real ledger source without also wiring sourceLedgerEntryId at that time, the original violation would recur under a different disguise.

crossCuttingRisks: All 8 MAJOR_NON_BLOCKING certification findings remain DEFERRED_NON_BLOCKING (21-major-finding-dispositions.json) - none was in this phase's scope, but none was fixed either.

DSGR's known-package regression check still shows a non-zero materialUnitsWithoutClaimReviewItem count due to a pre-existing, disclosed fixture-versioning artifact unrelated to this phase's fixes (22-known-package-regression.json) - a fresh, permanently-committed DSGR fixture would let this be re-verified honestly.

The known-package regression was run against the OLDER direct-pipeline-call pattern (runSemanticCoverageAudit + recordClaimReviewsFromDocumentCoverage called directly), not through the NEW live orchestrator BLOCKER-10 introduced - the two are logically equivalent by construction (the orchestrator calls the same functions in the same order) but this equivalence was not independently re-verified at full package scale through the new boundary specifically.

Certification-artifact-immutability near-miss (documented in 25-test-quality-gates.json): a pre-existing certification script's own hardcoded output path was discovered mid-phase to silently overwrite a frozen certification artifact when re-run. Caught and reverted before commit this time, but this specific script (scripts/phase-3f1-6-known-package-regression.ts) will do the same thing again if any future phase re-runs it without first copying or redirecting its output path - worth fixing in a future phase, not attempted here since editing a script under the frozen certification's own reference does not itself violate immutability but was judged out of this phase's bounded scope.
recommendedNextPhaseFocus: Phase 3F.1.6.RC (Targeted Foundation Recertification) should independently re-attack exactly the 11 previously-failed/coupled trust boundaries (E, H, J, K, L, plus the cross-cutting invariant #35 scope decision), verify each of the 11 dispositions above with its own adversarial tests against real data (not replaying this phase's own tests), and re-check only the boundaries materially touched by this remediation - not replay the 11 already-passing boundaries unnecessarily, per the phase charter's own Section 35 instruction.
